In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial inclusion bodies are cytotoxics in vivo, but not in vitro.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chaperones Dnak and GroEL are essential for the cell to tolerate the accumulation of misfolded proteins in the absence of the proteases Lon and ClpP.
the formation of inclusion bodies in vivo is not toxic per se, but the lack of the chaperones Dnak or GroEL makes them cytotoxic.
the chaperones are not essential for protein folding but are required to prevent the accumulation of misfolded proteins in the cytoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bacterial inclusion bodies are cytotoxics in vivo and that this toxicity can be minimized by functional chaperones.
in the absence of functional chaptersones DnaK and/or GroEL, misfolding of a model protein in vivo is highly detrimental for the cell.
